title: Normalized semilinear systems are closed under tensor and inverse image
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ a strict inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative rings. Let $\mathscr S(B)$ be the abelian category of $B_n$-module sheaves with semilinear transitions $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$ and componentwise compatible module maps [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Use its unbounded derived category. Call $M$ normalized when every transition-adjoint $\alpha^M_{m,n}:M_m\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n\to M_n$, $m\ge n\ge1$, is invertible; derived scalar extension uses the tensor/restriction adjunction of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Use the simultaneous enhanced section models of tensor and pullback in that node.

For normalized $P,Q\in D(\mathscr S(B))$, their fiberwise derived tensor system $T=P\otimes^LQ$ is normalized. More precisely its transition-adjoint is the composite
$$
(P_m\otimes^L_{B_m}Q_m)\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n
\xrightarrow{\sim}(P_m\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n)\otimes^L_{B_n}(Q_m\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n)
\xrightarrow{\alpha^P_{m,n}\otimes\alpha^Q_{m,n}}P_n\otimes^L_{B_n}Q_n.
$$
The first arrow is the canonical strong monoidal scalar-extension comparison, and these are the adjoints of the actual system transitions, with their quotient cocycles, not independently chosen reduction isomorphisms.

Let moreover $v:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C')\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi presented by a small site $\mathcal C'$, and put $C_n=v^{-1}B_n$ with its induced transitions. Then the system inverse image $v^*P$ is normalized over $(C_n)$: its transition-adjoint is $v^{-1}\alpha^P_{m,n}$ under the canonical comparison
$$(v^{-1}P_m)\otimes^L_{C_m}C_n\cong v^{-1}(P_m\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n).$$
These statements hold for unbounded complexes without flatness of the transition ring maps.

proof.text: Use the enhanced semilinear-section model to represent the actual tensor transition. For m≥n, the transition-adjoint of the fibrewise tensor system is obtained by first applying the derived scalar extension along B_m→B_n to P_m⊗^L_{B_m}Q_m and then applying the two cartesian transition-adjoints. The derived tensor pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], specialized to the identity topos and the coefficient map B_m→B_n, gives the canonical first isomorphism in the displayed formula. The two remaining factors are α^P_{m,n} and α^Q_{m,n}, hence are invertible by normalization. The section model in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] identifies this composite with the adjoint of the actual semilinear transition, rather than with a separately selected reduction isomorphism.

proof.text: The scalar-extension comparisons are coherent for a triple m≥n≥r: the two ways of extending from B_m to B_r are identified by the associativity comparison of derived extension of scalars, and the naturality of α^P and α^Q makes the two composites of the displayed tensor formula equal. The quotient cocycle for the tensor system is therefore the image of the quotient cocycles of P and Q under the enhanced tensor construction. Since the semilinear-section statement supplies simultaneous tensor models and says that cartesian sections are exactly normalized systems, these coherent invertible adjoints prove that P⊗^LQ is normalized.

proof.text: For a morphism of topoi v and C_n=v^{-1}B_n, use the inverse-image section model of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. At each m≥n, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives the canonical comparison (v^{-1}P_m)⊗^L_{C_m}C_n ≅ v^{-1}(P_m⊗^L_{B_m}B_n), with no flatness assumption on the coefficient map. Under this comparison the transition-adjoint of v^*P is exactly v^{-1}α^P_{m,n}; it is invertible because inverse image preserves isomorphisms. Naturality of the comparison and of the original quotient cocycle gives the cocycle for v^*P, so the section model identifies v^*P as normalized.
